summary: Feed s093_single to APM is degraded due to 10.7% packet loss (196/1838 TCP packets with missing data, threshold 1%). All other visibility checks (duplicates, one-way, VLAN, encryption, tool overload) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: Upstream capture is dropping packets before the packet broker/tool - most likely SPAN/mirror port oversubscription and buffer exhaustion during bursts. 10.66% TCP gaps indicates the SPAN cannot handle peak rate and is discarding packets, not a tool-side overload (tool_overload healthy).
findings.impact_on_tool: APM will see incomplete TCP streams, failed reassembly, inaccurate application latency/transaction timing, false retransmission alerts and missed performance anomalies due to 1 in 10 packets missing.

recommended_fix.why: SPAN ports drop under load due to small buffers and low priority vs production traffic; a passive TAP provides lossless, line-rate copy and eliminates the 10%+ loss seen here, restoring complete flows for APM without filtering needed since payload slicing is optional.
